title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE FRAMEWORK ACT ON LOW BIRTH RATE IN AN AGING SOCIETY
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE FRAMEWORK ACT ON LOW BIRTH RATE IN AN AGING SOCIETY

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Framework Act on Low Birth Rate in an Aging Society and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 1-2 (Persons Eligible for First Meeting Vouchers, etc.)
(1) A first meeting voucher under Article 10 (3) of the Framework Act on Low Birth Rate in an Aging Society (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as a "first meeting voucher") shall be paid to a newborn child in a lump sum according to the following classifications: <Amended 2024.3.26>
1. For a first-born child: A first meeting voucher worth two million won;
2. For a second or subsequent child: A first meeting voucher worth three million won.
(2) A person intending to apply for a first meeting voucher pursuant to Article 10 (5) of the Act shall submit an application for payment of a first meeting voucher prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare to the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply), accompanied by the following documents:
1. Documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare that can verify the personal information of the guardian;
2. A power of attorney and documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare that can verify the personal information of the agent (only where the guardian's agent applies);
3. Other documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare that are necessary to decide whether to pay a first meeting voucher.
(3) Where a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu who does not have jurisdiction over the newborn child's resident registration address receives an application for payment of a first meeting voucher, that official shall transfer the application and related documents without delay to the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the newborn child's resident registration address.
(4) The Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the newborn child's resident registration address who receives, by submission or transfer, an application for payment of a first meeting voucher and related documents pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) shall review whether the application is appropriate, etc., decide whether to pay a first meeting voucher, and pay it within one month from the date of the decision.
(5) A Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu who decides to make payment pursuant to paragraph (4) shall pay the first meeting voucher by issuing a voucher on the guardian's credit card, debit card, etc. that may be used to pay the costs necessary for raising the newborn child: Provided, That, for a recipient child under Article 10 (4) of the Act, payment shall be made by depositing cash into an account in the newborn child's name.
(6) A first meeting voucher may be used until the date falling two years after the date of the newborn child's birth. <Amended 2024.3.26>
(7) Detailed matters necessary for the procedures for payment of first meeting vouchers, etc., other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (6), shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare.

Article 2 (Formulation of Master Plans for Low Birth Rate and Aging Society)
(1) To efficiently formulate a master plan for low birth rate and aging society under Article 20 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "master plan"), the Minister of Health and Welfare shall, in advance, establish guidelines for preparing draft master plans and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies thereof. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15, 2022.2.3>
(2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall prepare draft master plans for matters under their respective jurisdiction in accordance with the guidelines for preparing draft master plans under paragraph (1) and submit them to the Minister of Health and Welfare; the Minister of Health and Welfare shall prepare a consolidated draft master plan and finalize the master plan in accordance with the procedures prescribed in Article 20 (2) of the Act. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15>
(3) Where the head of a relevant central administrative agency intends to amend matters under that agency's jurisdiction in a finalized master plan, the head shall prepare a proposed amendment to the master plan and submit it to the Minister of Health and Welfare, who shall submit it to the Committee on Low Birth Rate and Aging Society under Article 23 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee"). <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15>
(4) Where a master plan is finalized or amended pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3), the Minister of Health and Welfare shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15>

Article 3 (Formulation of Annual Implementation Plans)
(1) To efficiently formulate and implement annual implementation plans under Article 21 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plans"), the Minister of Health and Welfare shall establish guidelines for formulating implementation plans and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15>
(2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments shall formulate implementation plans for the following year for matters under their respective jurisdiction in accordance with the guidelines for formulating implementation plans under paragraph (1) and submit them to the Minister of Health and Welfare by December 31 each year. In such cases, the heads of local governments shall consult in advance with the Minister of Health and Welfare and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies regarding the contents of the implementation plans. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2009.3.12, 2010.3.15>
(3) Where implementation plans are finalized following deliberation by the Committee pursuant to Article 21 (3) of the Act, the Minister of Health and Welfare shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof without delay. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15>

Article 4 (Evaluation of Implementation Plans, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Health and Welfare shall prepare evaluation guidelines for evaluating the implementation performance of implementation plans under the former part of Article 21 (4) of the Act and, following deliberation by the Committee, notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof by January 15 each year. <Amended 2024.3.26>
(2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments shall evaluate the preceding year's implementation performance in accordance with the evaluation guidelines under paragraph (1) and submit the results to the Minister of Health and Welfare by the end of February each year. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15, 2024.3.26>
(3) The Minister of Health and Welfare shall consolidate the evaluation results submitted by the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments pursuant to paragraph (2) and, following deliberation by the Committee, notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments of the results by May 31 each year. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2010.3.15, 2024.3.26>
(4) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments shall reflect the evaluation results notified pursuant to paragraph (3) in the implementation plans for the following year. <Amended 2024.3.26>

Article 5 (Composition of the Committee)
(1) "Heads of relevant central administrative agencies prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 23 (4) 1 of the Act means the Minister of Finance and Economy, the Minister of Education, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Minister of Health and Welfare, the Minister of Employment and Labor, the Minister of Gender Equality and Family, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Minister of Planning and Budget, and the Minister of Government Legislation (hereinafter referred to as "ex officio members"). <Amended 2012.11.12, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2017.9.12, 2024.3.26, 2025.10.1, 2025.12.30>
(2) The term of office of a member appointed pursuant to Article 23 (4) 2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "appointed member") shall be 2 years: Provided, That the term of office of a member appointed to fill a vacancy shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term. <Amended 2009.3.12>
(3) An appointed member may continue to perform the duties of the office until a successor is appointed, even after the term of office under paragraph (2) expires. <Added 2021.11.30>
(4) Where deemed necessary, the chairperson of the Committee may have the heads of central administrative agencies and local governments related to the Committee's agenda items attend its meetings. <Amended 2012.11.12, 2021.11.30>
(5) The Committee shall have a vice chairperson, who shall be the secretary member designated by the President pursuant to Article 23 (5) of the Act. <Added 2017.9.12, 2021.11.30>
(6) The vice chairperson of the Committee shall serve on a full-time basis. <Added 2024.3.26>

Article 6 (Duties of the Chairperson)
(1) The chairperson of the Committee shall represent the Committee and exercise overall control over its affairs.
(2) Where the chairperson of the Committee is unable to perform the duties of the office, the vice chairperson shall act on behalf of the chairperson. <Amended 2017.9.12>

Article 7 (Meetings of the Committee)
(1) The chairperson of the Committee shall convene and preside over meetings of the Committee.
(2) To convene a meeting, the chairperson of the Committee shall notify each member and the heads of central administrative agencies and local governments attending the meeting pursuant to Article 5 (4), in writing, of the date, time, place, and agenda items of the meeting at least 7 days before it is held: Provided, That this shall not apply where urgent circumstances or other unavoidable grounds exist. <Amended 2012.11.12, 2021.11.30>
(3) A meeting of the Committee shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members, and resolutions shall be passed with the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.

Article 7-2 (Dismissal of Appointed Members)
The chairperson of the Committee may dismiss an appointed member if the member falls under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. Where the member is deemed unable to perform the duties of the office due to an illness requiring long-term treatment or other grounds;
2. Where the member has committed misconduct in connection with the duties of the office;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable to retain the position of appointed member due to neglect of duty, impairment of dignity, or other grounds;
4. Where the appointed member expresses that it is difficult for him or her to perform the duties of the office.

Article 8 (Operating Committee on Low Birth Rate and Aging Society)
(1) The Committee shall have an Operating Committee on Low Birth Rate and Aging Society (hereinafter referred to as the "Operating Committee") to review, coordinate, and consult in advance on agenda items to be submitted to the Committee and to support the Committee's activities. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2012.11.12, 2022.11.24>
(2) The Operating Committee shall consist of not more than 20 members, including 2 chairpersons, and 1 member other than the chairpersons shall serve as an executive member. In such cases, the executive member shall be a person designated by the President from among the members under paragraph (3) 2. <Amended 2022.11.24>
(3) The 2 secretary members under Article 23 (5) of the Act shall jointly serve as chairpersons of the Operating Committee, and its members shall be the following persons: <Amended 2006.6.12, 2008.2.29, 2009.3.12, 2010.3.15, 2012.11.12, 2022.11.24, 2024.3.26>
1. Vice ministers or deputy heads of the relevant central administrative agencies to which the ex officio members belong. In such cases, where an agency has more than 1 vice minister, the vice minister designated by the head of that agency shall serve;
2. Persons designated by the President from among the appointed members;
3. Persons jointly appointed by the chairpersons of the Operating Committee from among vice ministers or vice-minister-level public officials of relevant central administrative agencies related to policies on low birth rate and aging society.
(4) The Operating Committee shall have 1 executive secretary, who shall be designated by the Minister of Health and Welfare from among public officials of Grade III or public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Civil Service in departments of the Ministry of Health and Welfare related to policies on low birth rate and aging society. <Added 2012.11.12>
(5) The Operating Committee may establish and operate an advisory group composed of relevant experts where necessary to seek professional opinions on matters under its jurisdiction or to request research or surveys on specific tasks. <Amended 2022.11.24>
(6) Matters necessary for the composition, operation, and scope of duties, etc. of the Operating Committee and advisory group shall be determined by the chairperson of the Committee following a resolution of the Committee. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2012.11.12, 2022.11.24>

Article 9 (Secretariat)
(1) The Committee shall have a secretariat to support the smooth operation of the Committee and perform its substantive administrative affairs. <Amended 2017.9.12>
(2) The head of the secretariat shall be a person designated by the President upon the recommendation of the Minister of Health and Welfare from among public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Civil Service. <Amended 2022.11.24>
(3) Deleted <2022.11.24>
(4) The head of the secretariat shall exercise overall control over the affairs of the secretariat under the direction of the chairperson and direct and supervise its staff. <Added 2017.9.12, 2022.11.24>

Article 10 (Secondment of Public Officials, etc.)
(1) Where necessary for the operation of the Committee or the performance of the secretariat's affairs, the Committee may request the secondment or concurrent appointment of public officials of central administrative agencies or local governments, or executive officers, employees, or researchers of relevant private institutions, organizations, research institutes, etc. <Amended 2017.9.12>
(2) Where necessary for the operation of the Committee or the performance of the secretariat's affairs, the Committee may have experts in relevant fields serve as fixed-term public officials within the budget. <Amended 2013.11.20, 2017.9.12>

Article 11 (Allowances, etc.)
Members attending meetings of the Committee or the Operating Committee may be paid allowances, travel expenses, and other necessary expenses within the budget: Provided, That no such payments shall be made where public officials attend in direct connection with the duties under their jurisdiction. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2022.11.24>

Article 12 (Detailed Operating Rules)
Matters necessary for the operation of the Committee, other than those prescribed in this Decree, shall be determined by the chairperson of the Committee following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 13 (Entrustment of Survey and Research Duties)
(1) Pursuant to Article 29 (2) of the Act, the State may entrust survey and research duties concerning the evaluation of policies on low birth rate and aging society to an institution falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. A national or public research institution;
2. A government-funded research institution under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes;
3. A school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act (including affiliated research institutions);
4. A local government-funded research institute under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Local Government-Funded Research Institutes.
(2) Where the State entrusts duties pursuant to Article 29 (2) of the Act, it shall publicly notify the entrusted institution and the details of the entrusted duties.

Article 14 (Processing of Unique Identifying Information)
Special Self-Governing City Mayors, Special Self-Governing Province Governors, and heads of Sis/Guns/Gus may process materials containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's license numbers, or alien registration numbers specified in the subparagraphs of Article 19 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where it is unavoidable for the performance of affairs concerning the provision of first meeting vouchers under Article 1-2.
